_what: LH-REQ robot quality table. A COMMITTED INPUT FILE, read by the policy, never a constant in policy code: refilling it is a data update that leaves the frozen policy byte-identical.
_ruling: D143 ruling A, D6-compliant: the table is FITTED ON THE DEV SPLIT (28 questions) and LH-REQ robots DRAW ONLY FROM THE EVAL SPLIT (69 questions) in every run. The EVAL and all-97 blocks are recorded for reference and MUST NOT be read by the policy.
_precision_warning: The DEV fit rests on 28 questions, with cloud D2 at 7 of 28 and cloud RECENT at 3 of 28, so the fitted numbers carry wide Wilson intervals. They are recorded beside every point estimate as the user ruled; a freeze that quotes the point estimate alone would overstate its own precision.
_device_stack: D87, StudyO-Q4 4B-I x RECENT, the ORIN2 in-process harness. NOT the ORIN3 vLLM stack used for single-shot; the two must not be placed side by side as one device's numbers.
_cloud_source: results/sember/study_acc2/acc2_requests.jsonl, which carries question_id, rep, split and correct per request, so both sides are computed on the SAME questions. Ids join on a 60-character prefix, 97 of 97 found.
_controls_passed: the all97 cloud D2 figure reproduces the committed d2_acc of 45.3608 in lh_req_definition.json
the all97 cloud RECENT figure reproduces the committed recent_acc of 21.6495
the device filter reproduces D87 exactly: 845 questions, 277 correct, 32.781 percent
DEV 28 and EVAL 69 reproduce the committed per_split, with zero unmatched ids under case folding of BOTH sides
_mismatched_denominator_note: An earlier version of this comparison subtracted split-subset device figures from the cloud's all-97 aggregate. Every arithmetic check passed and the result was wrong in direction. Both sides here are on the same question set.

_dev_coincidence.fact: on the DEV split, cloud RECENT and the device both score 3 of 28, 0.107143
_dev_coincidence._note: the aggregates agree and the ITEMS do not: the two score 3 correct each but share only 1 question, so the equality is arithmetic rather than agreement. It matters because the device entry in the policy's LH-REQ fit is this same 0.107143 standing in for device-on-D2, and a reader could take the coincidence as corroboration that the substitution is sound. It is not evidence either way.
_dev_coincidence._conclusion_that_does_hold: at the AGGREGATE, which is what the policy consumes, a 32B restricted to the recent window scores the same as the 4B on these questions, so model size buys nothing at fixed representation here. That is the measured statement; 'the two models agree' is not.

_device_entry_substitution: the policy's device value for LH-REQ is the 4B x RECENT measurement. The consumer (rollout.py, the C6 mirror) asks for device accuracy on D2, and NO device-on-D2 result exists on these questions: StudyO-Q4 holds exactly three device arms, 4B-I x RECENT, 4B-T x RICH and 8B-I x RICH, and D87 fixes the comparator at 4B-I x RECENT. Declared, not implied.
